correctness.rationale: Jia--Ji's full arXiv text gives \(\Psi_A(aI)=(a-1)(I-A-aA^*)^{-1}+I\) and proves the denominator is invertible for every \(a\in\mathbb T\). If two distinct nonidentity values have scalar images, then \(I-A-aA^*\) is scalar for each; subtraction forces \(A^*\), hence \(A\), scalar. Conversely scalar \(A=\alpha I\) makes the whole circle scalar. Substitution gives the stated fractional-linear formulas; the sign of \(1-2\operatorname{Re}\alpha\) puts the disk parameter inside \(\mathbb D\), and solving for \(\alpha\) proves surjectivity and uniqueness onto the Möbius/anti-Möbius stabilizer of 1. The same primary paper explicitly identifies \(A=0\) with identity, \(A=I\) with adjoint/conjugation, and proves these are exactly the orthogonality-preserving cases.
correctness.risk: The classification is for Jia--Ji's normalized \(\Psi_A\) factor; arbitrary order automorphisms also carry exterior unitary or conjugate-unitary factors.

value.rationale: The center is a canonical subset of the matrix algebra, and identifying exactly which exotic order automorphisms preserve it gives a clean rigidity test and a complete one-complex-parameter boundary dynamical model. The two-probe criterion is a structural lemma, not a numerical check.
value.risk: The deduction is short once the Jia--Ji scalar formula is available.

final_claim: For the normalized Jia--Ji automorphisms \(\Psi_A\) of matrix partial isometries, the scalar unitary circle is invariant exactly when \(A=\alpha I\) with \(1-2\operatorname{Re}\alpha\ne0\); already two distinct nonidentity scalar probes with scalar images force this. In the positive and negative definiteness regimes, the induced circle action is respectively every Möbius and every anti-Möbius disk automorphism fixing \(1\), uniquely parametrized by \(A\); the orthogonality-preserving endpoints are the identity and conjugation.
limitations: No assertion is made about center preservation after arbitrary exterior \(\Delta_{CD}\) factors unless they are separately normalized.
